newsitem.title: UK: Glaxo drops after Zantac patent ruling.
newsitem.headline: Glaxo drops after Zantac patent ruling.

text.p: Shares in Glaxo Wellcome Plc dropped in early trading on Monday after the drug group said a U.S. court had ruled in favour of a maker of generic copies of its ulcer drug Zantac.
The stock was down 13-1/2p at 10.76-1/2 stg by 0803 GMT.
The company said the U.S. court of appeals had ruled in favour of Novopharm Inc in a patent action brought by Glaxo to prevent Novopharm marketing a generic form of Zantac.
The ruling will allow Novopharm to market a version of the drug, which at one time accounted for more than half Glaxo's total sales, from July 1997.
Glaxo added that it had for some time highlighted the likelihood of generic competition to Zantac in the U.S. from July and that it was encouraged by the rapid growth of new products.
By 0732 GMT the stock had rallied from its initial tumble to be down just 5p at 10.85 stg.
